subject: Reporting structured and unstructured effects of BYM model

messages.author: 461a0c7d7557dffc
messages.subject: Reporting structured and unstructured effects of BYM model
parts:
Dear list

Working with simple model from tutorial:

data(Germany)
g = system.file("demodata/germany.graph", package="INLA")
source(system.file("demodata/Bym-map.R", package="INLA"))
summary(Germany)
prior.iid = c(1,0.01)
prior.besag = c(1,0.001)
initial.iid = 4
initial.besag = 3

formula1.bym = Y ~ f(region, model = "bym", graph = g,
                     param = c(prior.iid, prior.besag),
                     initial = c(initial.iid, initial.besag)) + x
result1.bym = inla(formula1.bym,family="poisson",data=Germany,E=E)

When I want to get the (exponentiated) fixed effects for the covariate x I use

exp(result1.bym$summary.fixed)

In some publications (Here is one example, bottom of Table 2) I see random effects (structured and unstructured, with 95% CI) being also reported.

Where can I find them in the result object?

On Sat, 2014-10-18 at 07:45 -0700, Radoslaw Panczak wrote:
> Dear list
>
> Working with simple model from tutorial:
>
> data(Germany)
> g = system.file("demodata/germany.graph", package="INLA")
> source(system.file("demodata/Bym-map.R", package="INLA"))
> summary(Germany)
> prior.iid = c(1,0.01)
> prior.besag = c(1,0.001)
> initial.iid = 4
> initial.besag = 3
>
> formula1.bym = Y ~ f(region, model = "bym", graph = g,
> param = c(prior.iid, prior.besag),
> initial = c(initial.iid, initial.besag)) + x
> result1.bym = inla(formula1.bym,family="poisson",data=Germany,E=E)
>
>
> When I want to get the (exponentiated) fixed effects for the covariate
> x I use
>
> exp(result1.bym$summary.fixed)

you can transform the posterior marginal of each fixed effect using
inla.tmarginal,

like

> exp.fixed.maginal = inla.tmarginal(function(x) exp(x), result1.bym
$marginals.fixed[[1]])
> plot(exp.fixed.maginal)



Best
H
